summary: This sermon explores the biblical model of servant leadership, arguing that effective Christian leaders must balance three elements: responsibility, authority, and privilege. Using Philippians 2 and John 15 as anchor texts, the speaker contends that Jesus exemplified this balance by emptying himself as a servant yet leading with divine authority, and now calls his followers to the same pattern. The message warns against various dysfunctional leadership styles that emerge when these three elements fall out of alignment, emphasizing that the ultimate goal of servant leadership is not merely producing results but reproducing Christ-like leaders in others.
key_points: Servant leadership is not either/or but both/and: we serve while we lead
Authority, responsibility, and privilege must stay in balance for healthy leadership
Imbalances create dysfunction: narcissism, codependency, micromanagement, burnout, or hireling mentality
The highest level of leadership is reproduction—making others better leaders, not just getting results
Self-care is stewardship, not selfishness; leaders cannot give what they have not received
big_idea: Christ calls us to servant leadership that balances authority, responsibility, and privilege so we can reproduce lasting fruit by making others into Christ-like leaders.
title: We Are the Church: The Servant Leader
